title: Tensor compatibility of the raw rational continuous realization
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $A$ and uniformizer $\varpi$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension], and a separated finite-type scheme $T$ over $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$, where $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}k$ [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. Put $B_T=\varprojlim_n(A/\varpi^n)_T$ and $E_T=B_T[1/\varpi]$, with localization the sheaf colimit of repeated multiplication by $\varpi$. Use the small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], and the raw rationalized category $\mathcal C_E(T)=D^b_c(T,E)$ of [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi]. Tensor $\otimes^L_E$ and its unit $\mathbf1_E$ in this category are exactly the completed-integral, rationalized operations of [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom].

Let $I_{T,E}$ be the finite-stage identity-on-integral-objects equivalence of [lem-fd-rational-coefficient-category-comparison] from $\mathcal C_E(T)$ to the PBC raw rationalization, and let $J^{\mathrm{pbc}}_{T,E}$ be the t-exact continuous-coefficient realization of [lem-per-continuous-rational-derived-realization]. Set $J_{T,E}=J^{\mathrm{pbc}}_{T,E}I_{T,E}$. Its values are bounded complexes of $E_T$-module sheaves with stratified locally finite free cohomology, in the ambient derived category of module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category].

There are canonical natural isomorphisms
$$J_{T,E}(P\otimes^L_E Q)\xrightarrow{\sim}J_{T,E}(P)\otimes^L_{E_T}J_{T,E}(Q),\qquad J_{T,E}(\mathbf1_E)\xrightarrow{\sim}E_T[0]$$
for all $P,Q\in\mathcal C_E(T)$. These comparisons make $J_{T,E}$ symmetric strong monoidal: they commute with associators, unitors and the signed symmetry. On integral representatives they are the coefficient-extension comparisons from the completed derived tensor to ordinary derived tensor after localization; on localized arrows $f/\varpi^n$ they use $J(f)/\varpi^n$. They commute with finite field extension $E\subset F$, where on the ambient side extension means $F_T\otimes^L_{E_T}-$ and on the raw rational side it is the scalar extension in [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi].

source.place: Proposition 6.8.14(2) and Remark 6.8.15; tensor-compatible formulation for the specified completed operations. Also Hemo--Richarz--Scholbach Proposition 5.5 and Theorem 7.7 (natural coefficient-extension comparison). The extra coherence assertions are an agent formulation.

proof.text: The field $k$ is Noetherian (its only ideals are $0$ and $k$). Thus [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] and [lem-kun-dimension-finite-type] make $T$ Noetherian and finite-dimensional; $\ell$ is invertible since $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}k$. Also [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-over-affine] makes $T$ qcqs. All scheme hypotheses of the comparison and tensor lemmas below therefore hold. Abbreviate $B=B_T$ and $V=E_T$. By [lem-fd-rational-coefficient-category-comparison], $I_{T,E}$ is the identity on the common integral objects and on their localized Hom groups. By [lem-per-continuous-rational-derived-realization], the composite realization consequently has the formula $J(QM)=L_E(M):=V\otimes^L_B M$ and $J(f/\varpi^n)=\varpi^{-n}L_E(f)$. Here $Q$ denotes raw rationalization. These are the actual completed and continuous coefficient sheaves; no discrete constant $E$-sheaf is substituted.

source.place: Proposition 6.8.14(2), Remark 6.8.15; verify the scheme hypotheses of the already recorded realization

proof.text: Let $M,N$ be integral representatives and write $T_B(M,N)=M\otimes^L_BN$ and $\widehat T(M,N)=M\widehat\otimes^L_A N$. The latter is exactly the tensor on representatives in [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]. Apply [lem-fix-constructible-tensor-completion]: the canonical quotient-tower map $\chi_{M,N}:T_B(M,N)\to\widehat T(M,N)$ is a natural isomorphism. In particular the ordinary tensor is itself integral constructible, since it is isomorphic to the prescribed constructible completed tensor. On flat-term K-flat representatives $P,Q$, $\chi$ has level-$n$ component $x\otimes y\mapsto\bar x\otimes\bar y$ and zero shifted Roos component. This specifies the comparison used below; it is not an arbitrary isomorphism of the two objects.

source.place: Lemma 6.5.5, pp. 49–50; Definition 3.4.10 and Lemma 3.4.12(4), pp. 22–23

proof.text:
Regard $B\to V$ as a morphism of ringed topoi with underlying identity geometric morphism. By [lem-sfb-ringed-derived-monoidal-comparisons], its ordinary derived scalar extension $L_E$ has natural coherent isomorphisms $t_{M,N}:L_E(T_B(M,N))\to L_E(M)\otimes^L_VL_E(N)$ and $e:L_E(B[0])\to V[0]$. Define
$$\tau_{M,N}=t_{M,N}\circ L_E(\chi_{M,N}^{-1}):L_E(\widehat T(M,N))\xrightarrow{\sim}L_E(M)\otimes^L_VL_E(N).$$
The single-stratum perfect model $A[0]$ in [lem-weil-pbc-integral-stratified-perfect-characterization] shows that $B[0]$ is integral constructible and derived complete. The quotient-completion unit in [lem-weil-pbc-constant-completion-equivalence] therefore identifies $B[0]$ with $R\lim_n(A/\varpi^n)_T[0]$. This is the coefficient unit system, so [lem-pur-completed-operation-tower-substitution] identifies the completed tensor unit and its action unitors with $B[0]$ and the coefficient actions. Therefore $e$ gives the claimed unit comparison. Naturality and invertibility follow from those of $t,e,\chi$.

source.place: Tag 07A4 (lemma-pullback-tensor-product), with the normalized composition and unit comparisons; Bhatt–Scholze Definition 3.4.10 for the completed unit

proof.text: Check the passage from ordinary to completed tensor before rationalizing. Choose simultaneous flat-term K-flat representatives $P,Q,H$. Their total tensors can be used again as K-flat representatives by [lem-pur-kflat-total-tensor-model]. The normalized substitution statement [lem-pur-completed-operation-tower-substitution] identifies every iterated completed tensor with the derived limit of the corresponding whole quotient-tensor system; its associator, unitors and symmetry are the limits of the actual system maps. Insert the maps $\chi$ of Step 2 at the inner and outer tensors. For associativity, the two resulting maps from $\operatorname{Tot}((P\otimes_BQ)\otimes_BH)$ into the reassociated triple quotient tower have, at every quotient, the identical formula $(x\otimes y)\otimes z\mapsto\bar x\otimes(\bar y\otimes\bar z)$. These are equal maps of the whole strict quotient diagrams, with zero shifted component in the maps into their Roos limits, so applying the functorial derived limit preserves their equality. For either unitor the same calculation is $b\otimes x\mapsto\bar b\bar x$ or $x\otimes b\mapsto\bar b\bar x$; for symmetry it is $x\otimes y\mapsto(-1)^{pq}\bar y\otimes\bar x$ in degrees $p,q$. Thus $\chi$ intertwines the specified ordinary and completed structural maps. This compares actual diagram maps, rather than inferring equality of derived maps from equality of their separate reductions.

source.place: Definition 3.4.10 and Lemma 6.5.5; explicit quotient-system check of the structural comparisons

proof.text: Since $L_E$ is symmetric strong monoidal for ordinary tensor, [lem-sfb-ringed-derived-monoidal-comparisons] and Step 4 imply that $\tau,e$ satisfy the associator, both unit and signed-symmetry diagrams for the completed tensor. Now descend these transformations to the raw localization. In [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi] objects are unchanged and an arrow is a fraction of an integral arrow. For $u/\varpi^a$ and $v/\varpi^b$, the tensor-arrow formula of [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom] and the realization formula of Step 1 multiply both routes through the naturality square by $\varpi^{-(a+b)}$. The integral naturality square therefore proves the localized one; additivity treats sums. Changing a fraction representative gives the same result because multiplication by $\varpi$ becomes invertible in the target. The coherence equations remain equalities after localization. Since $I_{T,E}$ is the identity on integral objects and localized arrows, these are comparisons for the stated functor $J_{T,E}$ itself.

source.place: Proposition 6.8.14(2) and Remark 6.8.15; explicit descent of the natural transformations to raw Hom localizations

proof.text:
For a finite field extension $E\subset F$, put $C=\widehat{\mathcal O}_{F,T}$ and $W=F_T$. By [lem-weil-finite-free-completed-scalar-comparison], ordinary $C\otimes^L_B M$ is canonically identified with the prescribed completed integral scalar extension by its actual quotient-completion map $\chi_{F/E,M}$. The field-stage equivalence uses the inverse of this same map by [lem-fd-rational-coefficient-category-comparison]. Thus, under these specified comparisons, both scalar-then-realize and realize-then-scalar are ordinary iterated extension of rings along $B\to C\to W$ and $B\to V\to W$. The comparison is the balanced tensor identification
$$W\otimes_C^L(C\otimes_B^L M)\cong W\otimes_B^L M\cong W\otimes_V^L(V\otimes_B^L M).$$
The composition comparisons and their identity normalizations are those of [lem-sfb-ringed-derived-monoidal-comparisons]. No finite quotient coefficient map is assumed flat, and a uniformizer of $E$ is not identified with a uniformizer of $F$.

source.place: Lemma 6.8.2(1), Definition 3.4.10; Stacks Tag 0D6D for composition of ordinary derived extension of rings

proof.text: It remains to compare the tensor maps through that scalar identification. The canonical completed tensor scalar comparison is not left unspecified: [lem-pur-scalar-extension-tower-coherence] identifies it with the limit of the scalar-association tensor maps of the entire quotient systems, including every transition. Insert the completion maps from Steps 2 and 6. At an $\mathcal O_F/\varpi_F^m$ quotient, both routes send $c\otimes(x\otimes y)$ to $(c\otimes x)\otimes(1\otimes y)$; their maps from the uncompleted tensor to the Roos complex have zero shifted component. These are equal diagram maps, so their limits agree. Consequently the completed scalar/tensor square becomes the ordinary scalar/tensor square. The latter commutes, including its unit square, because the composition comparison of derived pullbacks is monoidal by [lem-sfb-ringed-derived-monoidal-comparisons]. The unit calculation is $c\otimes b\mapsto cb$. Applying $W\otimes_C^L-$, and then localizing the arrows as in Step 5, proves the required compatibility of $\tau$ and $e$ with $W\otimes_V^L-$. For a tower of fields the same balanced maps satisfy the composition identity by those two cited statements. This proves all the claimed tensor, unit, coherence and finite-extension assertions.

source.place: Tags 07A4 and 0D6D; quotient-system normalization of the completed scalar comparison and the explicit balanced-map square
